[Public Transit] Use openNewTabFast() in tests with a page Station

Replace ChromeTabUtils#newTabFromMenu() with
CtaPageStation#openNewTabFast() in 6 test classes that already hold a
page Station, and keep the new tab's Station where the test uses it.

NavigateTest#testOpenAndNavigate loads the page with
loadWebPageProgrammatically() so the Station matches the tab before
opening the new tab. It no longer asserts the tab count itself:
openNewTabFast() waits for a tab to be added to the regular TabModel
(TabAddedCondition) and for the new tab to be selected and loaded.

The changed tests in FullscreenManagerTest,
ChromeHttpAuthHandlerTest#authDialogSuppressedOnBackgroundTab and
NavigationHandlerTest#testCloseChromeAtHistoryStackHead are
@DisabledTest, so CQ doesn't run them. FullscreenManagerTest doesn't
keep the new tab's Station because it selects the old tab back without
arriving at a page Station (the browser controls hide in fullscreen).

WebUI Toolbar: Match Views handling of back/forward mouse buttons

The back/forward mouse buttons acted as clicks on WebUI toolbar
buttons, triggering reloads or inverted back/forward navigation.

Views toolbar buttons ignore these mouse buttons. On Windows, the
unhandled event becomes WM_APPCOMMAND, which navigates the active tab.
On other platforms, nothing happens.

Match this by intercepting these mouse buttons in the toolbar WebView's
PreHandleMouseEvent() so they never reach the page. On Windows, also
send the matching APPCOMMAND to ExecuteWindowsCommand().

The toolbar still gets focused when these buttons are clicked, but
I'll leave that for crbug.com/519327032.

6e14c6883bfc79413d4ae88039a21b648038fca9

02a03b4d55c2db6e2d2334d7b1310c11279300d9
parent
389542ca387d2e26c3edaee0a933ab92e28e83d8 [ diff ] 
[X11] Let the window manager follow touch-initiated window moves

Touch-dragging the custom frame (with "Use system title bar and
borders" off) did not move the window on X11 window managers such as
Openbox, while mouse drags did.

On a touch scroll in the caption, X11Window sends _NET_WM_MOVERESIZE
with no button. The window manager then grabs the core pointer and
follows its motion, but Chrome selects XI2 touch events and so owns
the touch sequence: the server never emulates pointer events for it,
and the window manager sees no motion. (Mutter tracks touches itself,
which is why GNOME was unaffected.)

When the move starts during a touch event, reject the touch with
XIAllowEvents(RejectTouch), so the server emulates pointer events for
it, and report the emulated button 1 as held so the window manager ends
the move when the finger is lifted. Qt's xcb backend starts
touch-initiated system moves the same way.

GTK: Make the primary background color opaque

Some GTK themes (e.g. Orchis) give the window a translucent background.
GetBgColor("") then returns a non-opaque color, which was used as-is for
kColorPrimaryBackground. Foreground colors are derived from it with
BlendForMinContrast(), which DCHECKs that the background is opaque, so
Chrome hit a DCHECK at startup with such themes.

Composite the window background over the frame color, as was already
done for the native toolbar color, so kColorPrimaryBackground is opaque
and matches kColorNativeToolbarBackground.

parent
9bb6315b8f22c690cb6ca60c33be97bc183a0e7a [ diff ] 
[X11] Don't hit test WM frames of ignored windows

During a tab drag, X11ScreenOzone::GetLocalProcessWidgetAtPoint() asks
WindowCache for the window under the cursor while ignoring the dragged
Chrome window. GetWindowAtPoint() skipped the ignored client window but
then fell back to its parent. With "Use system title bar and borders"
on Mutter X11 (mutter-x11-frames), that parent is the frame window,
which has a WM_NAME, so the frame was returned. It hid the Chrome
window under the cursor and the tab could not be attached to it.

When the point is over an ignored window, don't return any of its
ancestors either. Other children of those ancestors are still hit
tested.

[🌷] Fix HardwareDraw ImageReader teardown race

HardwareDraw previously closed its ImageReader from onImageAvailable()
or from the HardwareBuffer release callback while requestDraw() was
still finishing HardwareRenderer.syncAndDraw() and teardown on
sHardwareRequestThreadExecutor. Abandoning the BufferQueue while
RenderThread was still using the surface triggered a RenderThread crash
on Android 17 and Canary emulators, causing
NativePageBitmapCapturerTest#testWithNativePageHardwareBuffer to flake
~21% on android-17-x64-rel.

Detach the surface and destroy HardwareRenderer in a finally block, and
sequence discardFreeBuffers() plus HardwareBuffer/Image/ImageReader
closing on the single-threaded sHardwareRequestThreadExecutor so they
always run after HardwareRenderer teardown completes. Also defer
creating the Renderer until view recording succeeds, and guard against
null images or failed fence waits.

Based on https://crrev.com/c/8424233.

Test history: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Fandroid%5C%3Achrome_public_test_apk%21junit%3Aorg.chromium.chrome.browser.gesturenav%3ANativePageBitmapCapturerTest%23testWithNativePageHardwareBuffer
Failed build: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/android-17-x64-rel/40/overview

1005e5a2421c46a08f5971cc9f796f125a62bdf7 [ diff ] 
[WebAudio] Avoid re-querying a failed audio output device

When audio output authorization fails or times out during
RendererWebAudioDeviceImpl construction, HandleDeviceStatus() calls
Stop() and clears `sink_`. A subsequent MaybeCreateSinkAndGetStatus()
call then sees a null `sink_`, recreates it, and issues a second
blocking GetOutputDeviceInfo() query on the main thread.

Cache the output device status in `sink_status_` so
MaybeCreateSinkAndGetStatus() returns the cached non-OK status
immediately without recreating or re-querying the sink, while stopping
a working device preserves OK status so it can still reopen. Start()
still reopens `sink_` asynchronously so failures surface via
OnRenderError(). Callers such as AudioContext({sinkId}) and setSinkId()
now surface the initial failure instead of retrying onto placeholder
params, and WebAudio.AudioDestination.OutputDeviceStatus records that
cached status.

Based on https://crrev.com/c/8612789.

Changes:
- Track `sink_status_` on RendererWebAudioDeviceImpl and record it in
  HandleDeviceStatus() and MaybeCreateSinkAndGetStatus().
- Skip sink creation and GetSinkOutputDeviceInfo() in
  MaybeCreateSinkAndGetStatus() when `sink_status_` is not OK.
- Add unit tests covering cached error/timeout statuses, Start()
  reopening asynchronously after timeout, construction-param invariance
  on reopen after Stop(), and stricter single-query mock expectations.

Bug: 41475094
Test: content/renderer/media/renderer_webaudiodevice_impl_unittest.cc

0cb32569a13c212d75b4b305923a3f669f6ef490 [ diff ] 
Require unique element identifiers for all page actions

In the WebUI toolbar, page actions without an element_identifier in
PageActionPropertiesProvider are not registered with ElementTracker
[0][1], so CreateAndShowAnchoredMessage() previously fell back to
anchoring to kLocationBarElementId [2] instead of the icon (unlike Views
PageActionView, which anchors to itself [3]).

Define the missing element_identifier entries for
kActionSidePanelShowLensOverlayResults, kActionGlicContextualCueing,
kActionAnchoredContextualCue, and kActionFakePageActionForDebug. Enforce
at compile time that every page action defines a unique
element_identifier, drop the kLocationBarElementId fallback in
CreateAndShowAnchoredMessage() and null filtering in
GetAllElementIdentifiers(), and update WebUIPageActionControl tests.

[0] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/ad7c16dfdbe7f3d5bf54754bf31e75aebbfa8187:chrome/browser/ui/views/page_action/webui_page_action_control.cc;l=505-516
[1] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/ad7c16dfdbe7f3d5bf54754bf31e75aebbfa8187:chrome/browser/ui/webui/webui_toolbar/webui_toolbar_ui.cc;l=836-850
[2] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/ad7c16dfdbe7f3d5bf54754bf31e75aebbfa8187:chrome/browser/ui/views/page_action/webui_page_action_control.cc;l=631-641
[3] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/ad7c16dfdbe7f3d5bf54754bf31e75aebbfa8187:chrome/browser/ui/views/page_action/page_action_view.cc;l=614-615

NO_IFTTT=Only adding element_identifier to existing page actions and compile-time checks; no action IDs or histogram names changed.

[ios/web_view] Add prewarm support to ios_web_view_shell

Adds a way to exercise -[CWVWebView prewarm] manually:
1. A "Recreate and prewarm web view" menu item that replaces the current
   web view with a new one and calls -prewarm on it.
2. A "Recreate and load about:blank" menu item that replaces the current
   web view with a new one and loads about:blank in it, the way an
   embedder keeps a web view ready without -prewarm. Comparing the two
   shows the difference: after about:blank, the next page is the second
   back/forward item and Back returns to about:blank; after -prewarm, it
   is the first item.
3. After each address bar load, logs the time from the load request to
   commit and to finish, plus the back/forward list counts, canGoBack,
   and history.length.

[ios/web_view] Add -[CWVWebView prewarm]

Embedders that keep a CWVWebView ready today load about:blank, which
leaves a blank item at index 0 of the back/forward list, so
history.back() returns to a blank page. The window.open() initializer
avoids that but resets the BrowserState wide configuration provider.

-prewarm calls the new web::PrewarmWebView(), which creates the
WKWebView through the normal first navigation path, without resetting
the provider. No navigation item is created. It does nothing once a
load has started, so it is safe to call repeatedly.

A user agent set after -prewarm still applies to the first load
(covered by new ios_web_view_inttests).

On an iPhone 13 Pro Max, median load to commit dropped from about 275
ms to about 188 ms (en.wikipedia.org, 10 runs each), and history.length
stayed 1. Also running an empty script to start the web content process
early made no measurable difference, so -prewarm only creates the web
view.

10ec29d71e50de5222f137a925be5e33efab3d30 [ diff ] 
[glic] Resolve active BrowserWindowInterface dynamically for tools

GlicWebClientHandler owns GlicToolsHolder across Browser window
lifetimes (for example, when Glic is detached in a floating window).
Previously, CreateAiOverlayToolsForGlic resolved active_browser once
at Mojo pipe creation and stored a raw_ptr<BrowserWindowInterface> on
AiOverlayTools, triggering a MiraclePtr DanglingPtr crash if that
initial Browser window closed while Glic remained open.

Add a BrowserResolver overload to AiOverlayTools::Create() (and
subscribe to RegisterBrowserDidClose() for fixed-browser callers) so
Glic dynamically resolves the most recently activated normal
BrowserWindowInterface for the Profile on each tool call.

Bug: 587935179
Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter=*GlicChromeTools*

[Clipboard] Handle null streams from drag sources

A drag source can return TYMED_ISTREAM without an IStream pointer,
causing a CHECK failure when Chrome reads its file contents.

Treat the missing stream as a failed read and mark the medium TYMED_NULL
before releasing it. Preserve the existing filename handling and
valid-stream behavior.

Fixed: 583454016
